extracted.intended_audience: small business owners, founders, and solo/practical PR practitioners seeking guidance on outreach and press strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Practical public relations guidance for small businesses focused on when to pursue press, how to pitch, what story angles work, and how to build long-term media relationships. Emphasizes owned media and targeted, personalized outreach over mass distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-sized PR ambition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most small businesses don't need traditional PR; set ambitions appropriate to business scale (e.g., local or niche coverage rather than national). Avoid hiring expensive PR agencies or pursuing high-cost national campaigns that don't match business goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Owned media as foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Owned media (newsletter, podcast) more valuable than coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize building your own audience and expert reputation via owned channels. Long-term audience growth is more valuable than one-time press hits—use owned media as the foundation of your communications strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized to journalist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor pitches to a journalist's beat and interests: subject line should be a specific story idea + journalist's beat. Explain in Para 1 why the story matters to their readers. Avoid mass-blasting; remember journalists' beats, comment thoughtfully on others' work, and don't burn bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific story angle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, specific hook rather than generic announcements. Useful angles include local community impact, personal origin stories, industry trends you’re seeing first, counter-intuitive insights, and data from your customer base. Avoid generic 'we are excited to announce' wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honest, authentic framing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor authenticity over polish. Frame stories honestly—personal stories or genuine expertise resonate more than slick spin. Avoid 'look at me' stories and disingenuous hype.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term relationship building
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat media relationships as long-term: be a quotable source, send relevant items even when not actively pitching, comment thoughtfully on others' work, and maintain professional behavior to avoid burning bridges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch structure (Janet's Pitch Framework)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line: specific story idea + journalist's beat; Para 1: Why this story matters to their readers; Para 2: Your unique angle/expertise; Para 3: What you can offer (interview, data, exclusive); Sign-off: phone number, calendar link
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the prescribed paragraph structure and include concrete offers (interview, data, exclusivity). In sign-off include contact details and an easy scheduling link. A well-structured, concise pitch increases chance of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate outlets / when press helps
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue press that aligns with your audience and scale: local press for community-based businesses, niche industry publications, podcast appearances in your space, awards from credible bodies, and media-friendly origin stories. Targeted placements are more effective than broad coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ineffective tactics / when press wastes time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pitching national press for a purely local business, trying to 'go viral' without strategy, sending generic press releases without a hook, mass distribution without targeting, following up aggressively, wire-only distribution, and expensive retained-agency approaches that don't match needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story angles that work
rubrics_metrics.description: Story Angles That Work for Small Biz
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective angles include: local community impact; the personal story behind the business; an industry trend you're seeing first; a counter-intuitive insight from experience; data from your customer base; and award nominations or wins. Use these to craft the 'specific story angle' in your pitch.
